MY PATTERN STUDIO

My Pattern Pieces

Sort your shape cards, build long rows and swap patterns to solve.

Look, then try.

Ask a grown-up to cut along the card borders first. There are four of each piece: pink circles, yellow squares and purple triangles. Choose two or three shapes for your repeating row, and keep the rule in your head or whisper it as you place each card. When your row is long, hand it to someone else and ask them to continue it. If cutting is not possible, tear paper pieces or draw rows instead: the rule matters more than the cards.

Start drawing and writing below

Open the worksheet to print or save

An adult helps with cutting the pattern cards. Keep paper scraps away from younger children. Move gently during movement patterns: seated movements work too, and no jumping is needed.

Use a finger, stylus or mouse in each drawing box. Type below it, or ask a grown-up to write your words. Your work stays in this tab. Save before refreshing or leaving.

ACTIVITY 1

Sort my cards

Draw the pieces you chose for your pattern.

ACTIVITY 2

Build a long row

Draw your repeating row from the first piece to the last.

ACTIVITY 3

Solve a swap

Ask someone to start a row for you, then draw how you continued it.

Your ideas belong here. There is no score.

What are we learning?

Choosing, ordering and extending pieces builds sequencing and working memory. Explaining a rule to someone else checks that the pattern is clear.
